checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters, ED visits, urgent care visits, and hospital admissions in that window, including any cardiac chest-pain or MI-related presentations given the NSTEMI and ischemic heart disease history.
Falls and near-falls: review incident reports and nursing notes for the window, with attention to orthostatic symptoms since hydrochlorothiazide, lisinopril, metoprolol, and atenolol are all active.

Medication reconciliation: the chart lists both atenolol and metoprolol succinate as active, plus lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. Verify whether duplicate beta-blockers and antihypertensive regimens are intended and flag for prescriber review.

Antiplatelet and anticoagulant review: clopidogrel and prasugrel are both listed as active, which is a dual P2Y12 inhibitor concern. Confirm current prescribed antiplatelet regimen with cardiology and check for any bleeding events, bruising, GI bleeding, or anemia-related lab changes.
Statin review: simvastatin 20 mg and simvastatin 40 mg are both listed active. Check for duplicate entries, confirm the intended dose, and review lipid panel and any myalgia reports.

Tacrolimus (Envarsus) review: confirm prescriber, indication, start date (2026-04-04), and whether trough-level monitoring is occurring; check for tremor, renal function change, glucose change, and drug-interaction notes against the other active medications. Clarify indication since it is not linked to a listed condition.

Diabetes and glycemic control: review insulin use (Humulin 70/30) for hypoglycemia episodes, glucose logs, A1c trend, and whether dosing changed; reconcile with the prediabetes and metabolic syndrome entries, which may be outdated relative to insulin use.

Kidney function: review eGFR and creatinine trend, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, and potassium given diabetic kidney disease, proteinuria, lisinopril, HCTZ, and tacrolimus. Flag any changes for nephrology or prescriber review.
Blood pressure and heart rate: review home and clinic BP and pulse trends for the window against the antihypertensive regimen; check for symptomatic low readings or sustained elevation.

Respiratory status: review asthma control (albuterol and fluticasone use frequency, rescue inhaler refills, night symptoms, oxygen needs), and check for any respiratory ED visits. Note that albuterol and fluticasone started 2026-04-04 per the chart, so verify those start dates.

Weight and nutrition: obtain weight trend for the window given obesity (BMI 30+) and diabetes management, plus any appetite or intake concerns. Check dental and oral intake status given loss of teeth.
Function, ADLs, and cognition: review ADL/IADL assessments, mobility, and any cognitive screening changes; note new dependence or decline for IDT discussion.
Mood, social engagement, and attendance: review mood screening scores, attendance at PACE day center, missed appointments, and any caregiver strain or changes in living situation.

Care-plan items due: list any care-plan goals, reassessments, or referrals due in or before the 2026-11-30 review date, including eye exam, foot exam, and dental follow-up for diabetes care, and confirm allergy documentation (peanut angioedema) is current in the medication list and care plan.

Documentation hygiene: note the 'Allergic disposition' finding and the peanut angioedema allergy for the IDT summary, and flag any medication entries with no note or prescriber listed for reconciliation.
